llm.reason: A team is not a kind of player-attribute record, and the full containment with 0.002 coverage is just small-ID overlap between two unrelated primary-key ID pools.
A country cannot be a kind of or extension of a football match, and the Country IDs merely fall inside Match's dense 1..25979 key range, so the full containment is coincidental.
Match.col_001 is the match table's own primary key (match IDs), and a league is not a kind of match, so the ID overlap is coincidental.
Match.col_001 is the match table's primary key (match IDs), and its overlap with the 11 league IDs is coincidental since a match is not a league.
Country and League share the exact same 11-value ID pool with full coverage and one-to-one cardinality, and each league corresponds to exactly one country, a natural one-to-one extension link.
League.col_002 duplicates the same shared ID pool (identical to col_001) with full coverage, so it is an equally valid reference for the Country key.
League.col_001 shares the exact same 11-value ID pool as Country.col_001 with matching names (England Premier League ↔ England), showing the league key reuses the country key.

League.col_002 has exactly the same 11 values as Country.col_001 (full containment and coverage, one-to-one), and the league names (England Premier League, Germany 1. Bundesliga, Portugal Liga ZON Sagres) match the corresponding country names, confirming a real reference.

Match.col_001 is the match table's unique match_id (sequential 1–25979), and Team_Attributes.col_003 is a team_api_id already accepted to reference Team.col_002, so the ~99% containment is coincidental overlap of two unrelated ID ranges.

Player.col_001 is the player table's sequential primary key (1–11075), and the source column is a team_api_id referencing Team.col_002, so a team-attributes row cannot reference a player; the overlap is chance between ID ranges.

Match.col_008 is a team id (already accepted as Team.col_002), and its values (e.g. 9994, 8342) are team identifiers, not Player primary keys, so the high containment is coincidental overlap of two unrelated ID pools.

Match.col_009 has 299 distinct values almost fully contained in Player's primary key with many-to-one cardinality, and the Match rows carry per-player statistics/rating columns, consistent with a player_id reference into Player.

Team_Attributes col_002 is a team-level FIFA-style ID (285 distinct teams, repeated across dates), while Player_Attributes col_001 is a unique per-row player attribute ID; the full containment of small/medium integers into a dense 1..183978 key is coincidental and the entities (teams vs player attribute records) differ.

Team.col_002 is a team API-ID (unique per team, range ~1600–274k) while Match.col_001 is a dense sequential match ID 1–25979; the 98% containment is coincidental overlap of two dense integer ranges, and a team cannot reference a match.
